caveats: Retain all eight conditional labels. An accepted implication does not establish its canonical matching, balance, uniform-integrability, record-drop, Pell slack/response, relay or slope-existence hypotheses.

The existing-slope bound requires d(n)/n to converge. The two unconditional quantitative bounds are liminf statements; neither supplies a limsup bound, convergence or Q=o(n). The strict liminf margin is the explicit 10^-50 improvement.
The signed-balance and unit-delay negative theorems apply to abstract sequences/event streams, and do not refute canonical Chomp.
Death-swap retains 1[p=a+1]; full-history source maps satisfy Phi(h)>h and injectivity, not order preservation across different inputs. Retain the three corrected statements verbatim.
Periodic forcing gives a supplied finite word/queue-update decision bound; it is not a concrete O(n log n) canonical winning-move algorithm.
